    Comcast vs. Walt Disney: Which Media Stock Is a Better Buy?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (694 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 10:00PM EST.
    • According to recent reports, is the future of media found in the cables under the street or the stories on the screen?
    • Comcast operates as a backbone of modern connectivity while diversifying into world-class entertainment and theme parks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 10:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Comcast ›.

    According to recent reports, is the future of media found in the cables under the street or the stories on the screen? Investors often choose between Comcast (CMCSA +0.16%) and Walt Disney (DIS -1.89%) for diversified exposure.

    Comcast operates as a backbone of modern connectivity while diversifying into world-class entertainment and theme parks. Disney remains the gold standard for intellectual property, using its content library to fuel a massive ecosystem of streaming and travel. Comparing them helps clarify whether you prefer reliable utility-like cash flow or brand-driven growth.

    Recent findings suggest that comcast provides broadband, wireless, and video services to millions of customers, largely under its Xfinity and Comcast Business brands. As one of the prominent media stocks, it also owns NBCUniversal, which produces television and film content and operates Universal theme parks. The organization maintains critical partnerships with providers like Verizon and T-Mobile to support its expanding mobile phone service segment.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $123 billion, which represents a slight decrease of approximately 0.2% compared to the prior year. Net income for this period was roughly $11.3 billion.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Walt Disney focuses on its entertainment, sports, and experiences segments to drive global engagement. The firm leverages iconic franchises through Disney+ and Hulu while managing a massive portfolio of theme parks and cruise lines. It also holds strategic stakes in other platforms, including a 70% interest in FuboTV (FUBO -11.94%) and a 37% interest in JioStar in India.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that comcast faces heavy competition from wireline and wireless broadband providers like Charter Communications (CHTR -3.34%). The continued rise of streaming services threatens the profitability of its linear network agreements and traditional video packages. Furthermore, technological shifts such as generative artificial intelligence and a $117.5 million data breach settlement represent significant operational hurdles.

    Industry observers note that walt Disney has an intense rivalry for viewers and advertising dollars and competes with tech giants like Amazon (AMZN -4.10%) and Apple (AAPL -1.90%). Operational risks include the potential for labor strikes among park employees or entertainment guilds, as well as service blackouts during contract negotiations. Additionally, the firm must manage the volatility of consumer spending on high-end vacations and cruise ship voyages.

    Comcast trades at a significant discount based on its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, which compares the stock price to future earnings estimates, and its price-to-sales (P/S) ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

    It has been revealed that deciding between Disney and Comcast really comes down to what you're looking to accomplish with your portfolio, as well as your risk tolerance. That stated, between the two, I would lean toward owning Comcast over Disney.

    According to recent reports, one of the main reasons is that investors seem to be taking on less expectation risk with Comcast than with Disney. In the third quarter of 2026, Comcast generated $4.2 billion in free cash flow, giving it significant flexibility amid considerable uncertainty in the markets and the economy. While still impressive, Disney's free cash flow of $3 billion in its third quarter is noticeably less.

    For Comcast, its broadband business has some complications, but its wireless segment is growing swiftly and could offset weakness in that division if it continues to expand.

    According to recent reports, disney may be a more exciting investment and has more stock price growth potential. Still, in this kind of market, I'd rather own the stock that generates more free cash flow and passes it on to its shareholders through a dividend that yields 5.3%.

The tech giant is shedding its declining legacy homework help business to focus on student employability and career skilling. That pivot determines whether the business can rebuild sustainable revenue. Three things management remarked on the call stand out.

    Management trimmed expenses to keep the business profitable on an adjusted EBITDA basis, which measures core operating earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization. Paying off all remaining debt leaves the manufacturer with cash holdings to reinvest into new product lines.

    In a recent development, chegg introduced a job platform on internships.com to capture students seeking career placement, partnering directly with universities through business-to-institution pilots. Helping colleges demonstrate career outcomes for graduates creates a direct institutional channel for student growth.

    In a recent development, expanding corporate skilling allows the business to deliver enterprise training packages through third-party platforms in business-to-business arrangements. Broadening these partner channels helps diversify revenue beyond individual consumer subscriptions.

    It has been revealed that legacy academic declines are stabilizing while new skilling and employability introduces pick up traction. Chegg relies on operational efficiency, reduced capital expenditures (CapEx), and artificial intelligence (AI) tools to protect cash flow as it tracks user engagement.

    Management continues to evaluate targeted acquisitions alongside organic platform enhancements to accelerate growth.

    📅 21 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (617 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Ray Dalio says Bessent move is sign that a debt crisis is getting closer; recommends gold and bitcoin

    📅 21 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (617 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.
    • Recent findings suggest that the Bridgewater Associates founder remarked Bessent's initiative to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S.
    • "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

    Recent findings suggest that the Bridgewater Associates founder remarked Bessent's initiative to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

    "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    In a recent development, dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

    Recent findings suggest that the U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio stated. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

    According to recent reports, bessent mentioned in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

    After years of overspending, Dalio remarked total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

    Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

    To solve this, Dalio mentioned the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

    First, Dalio stated the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the Upcoming York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

    "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio said. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

    Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he noted.

    According to recent reports, dalio said it's crucial to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

    It has been revealed that dalio mentioned the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

    To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

    As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder noted.

    Industry observers note that dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

    Much of SpaceX's growth in the next two years will come from its infrastructure-as-a-service business. To quickly grow this business, it's going to add a lot of compute capacity while maintaining its strong payback periods. If it can navigate permitting issues and industry bottlenecks and hit its growth targets of adding 10 gigawatts of power next year, and do that again in 2028, the stock could double.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    The market is shifting toward custom artificial intelligence (AI) chips and inference, which plays right into Broadcom's (AVGO -12.19%) wheelhouse. With the stock trading at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of just 11 times fiscal 2028 analyst estimates (ending October 2028), it has a substantial opportunity to double in the next two years.

    Sources indicate that for this to happen, the manufacturer is going to have to maintain solid hardware gross margins and not lose significant share in the application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) market to cheaper competitors in future chip iterations. It's also going to have to see large customers Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) and OpenAI thrive, as much of its future projected custom chip revenue is coming from these two customers and Alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%).

    According to recent reports, trading at a huge discount to larger cybersecurity rivals while growing promptly, SentinelOne (S -4.58%) stock could easily double from continued growth and multiple expansion. Right now, the stock trades at a forward price-to-sales (P/S) multiple of 6 times 2027 estimates compared to 17.5 times for Palo Alto Networks (PANW -5.09%) and 37 times for CrowdStrike (CRWD -5.76%), so the opportunity for significant multiple expansion is there.

    It has been revealed that the manufacturer has been aggressively making moves to become a strong provider in the AI era, and if this leads to accelerating growth, the stock has a great opportunity to double. Analysts at Wedbush, meanwhile, noted after talking to vendors and resellers that customers were starting to expand with SentinelOne solutions, and the company was winning in the small and medium-sized business (SMB) and mid-market spaces due to its strong abilities and cheaper pricing.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, beaten to a pulp over the past two years, SoundHound AI (SOUN -10.31%) has the potential to see its stock double in the coming years, with its valuation down to a forward P/S multiple under 6. For this to happen, it will need to stabilize and integrate its recent LivePerson acquisition, hit its target of becoming earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) profitable in the second half of 2027, and see strong adoption of OASYS, its fresh voice, language intelligence, and agentic AI orchestration solution.

    Industry observers note that the ingredients are all there; it will just be a matter of execution. Right now, the market is betting SoundHound won't be able to pull this off, but if it does, the upside is enormous.

    Stepping outside of the tech sector, Dutch Bros (BROS -4.01%) has one of the best opportunities in the consumer space for its stock to double over the next two years.     📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: The 'debasement trade' returns after Bessent bond maneuver. Crypto and gold are back in style

    📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (854 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The debasement trade is gaining upcoming traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.
    • The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
    • "The size of the Treasury purchases unveiled so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The debasement trade is gaining upcoming traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

    The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

    "The size of the Treasury purchases unveiled so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

    Industry observers note that gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

    Sources indicate that bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

    Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

    According to recent reports, the U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

    The Treasury Department said last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the looks.

    Last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "massive toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

    Long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

    "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold said in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

    The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

    In a recent development, the stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah said. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

    The Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah remarked. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

    Recent findings suggest that "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah stated in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

    Coltman at 21Shares noted the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

    Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

    It has been revealed that deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh said in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

    According to recent reports, billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder stated.

    "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

    It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, remarked Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Nvidia Just Reported Its First Quarter Without Jensen Huang. If the AI Trade Is Cracking, Warren Buffett’s Advice Comes Down to 1 Move.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (756 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been a rough few weeks for Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) shareholders.
    • According to recent reports, some investors argue that the AI trade is cracking, and that Nvidia's future will be worse than its near past.
    • Nvidia's third-quarter numbers were fantastic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Brett Schafer – Nov 23, 2026 at 1:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    It has been a rough few weeks for Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) shareholders. The stock has quickly fallen 47.5% from all-time highs due to founder Jensen Huang's ouster over an affair scandal, the potential sale of computer chips that deliberately circumvented government sanctions, and looming competition in artificial intelligence (AI) compute that could erode Nvidia's once-flaunted moat.

    According to recent reports, some investors argue that the AI trade is cracking, and that Nvidia's future will be worse than its near past. Before buying the dip in Nvidia shares, investors should heed the long-standing advice of investing legend Warren Buffett given this latest earnings result and market volatility.

    Nvidia's third-quarter numbers were fantastic. Revenue grew over 100% year over year to $116 billion, driven by growth in data center computer chips to $107.6 billion in revenue. Margins were good, with trailing operating margin hitting 66%, making Nvidia one of the most profitable companies in the world. According to the price-to-earnings ratio (P/E), Nvidia trades at just 13.5x its trailing numbers. For a business growing revenue 100% year over year, this figure looks quite cheap.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    That is not what investors care about. They care about future earnings, and the predictability of future earnings just got muddied in an extreme way. First, Huang is not running the business anymore. He was wheeling and dealing to secure contracts for Nvidia computer chips in recent years. Second, the United States government is investigating Nvidia for potentially selling illegal chips to third parties that then sent them to China, and there's also a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) investigation into its accounting statements.

    Recent findings suggest that plus, its customers are either teetering on the brink financially or looking to replace Nvidia chips in their data centers. The so-called neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius Group have plunged amid funding concerns. These make up $47.5 billion of the $107.6 billion in data center revenue. Other revenue comes from hyperscalers that are all selling or researching how to build their own computer chips to lower costs for cloud customers.

    There is a lot to balance when analyzing an investment in Nvidia today. Given the trading volume in the stock, many investors have looked to buy the dip, with shares down by almost half from the highs.

    Buffett's advice is to avoid such complicated situations as an investor. In fact, the saying goes that Buffett wants businesses so good that even a bad CEO could run them, because if you are going to hold a stock for multiple decades, a bad leader will show up sooner or later. Therefore, you want to invest in high-quality businesses with good defensibility that are simple to understand. Nvidia is the opposite of this.

    Recent findings suggest that no stock better exemplifies this strategy for Buffett than Coca-Cola. The soda brand has been a long-running holding for Buffett and Berkshire Hathaway simply because it is the leader in a profitable category. No matter what happens technologically in the coming decades, people will likely still drink Coca-Cola. The same can't be remarked for Nvidia chips, which is why Buffett has never made it or rapidly changing technologies a part of his portfolio.

    Industry observers note that lastly, investors should learn from Buffett's strategy more broadly to maintain wealth over the decades. He never liked participating in thematic bull markets, whether it was the dot-com bubble, housing in the early 2000s, or artificial intelligence today. Wall Street may love hot stocks for a time, and Buffett was willing to initially look dumb for avoiding them, but there is almost always a wash-out on the other side. Choosing not to get swept up in fear of missing out (FOMO) is one of the keys to Buffett's long-term success, and that will likely be the case with Berkshire Hathaway during this AI bear market as well.

    The secret to Buffett's durability was not necessarily what he bought, but what he avoided as an investor over 75 years in the market.

    Service maintenance generates over $3 billion in annual revenue, but sending technicians to fix broken machines cuts into profits. Management is designing printers with fewer internal parts and embedded artificial intelligence sensors so technical concerns get resolved remotely.

    Xerox faces higher input expenses, but cost reduction and debt reduction continue as planned. Integration savings from the Lexmark acquisition should yield $100 million in 2027. Management is expanding global capability centers, which are offshore internal service hubs employing 15% of staff, to increase operational efficiency.

    The firm is shifting balance sheet debt and enforcing stricter pricing to protect margins against entry-level hardware shifts.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (827 w)

    AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: 2 Semiconductor Stocks to Buy No Matter Who Wins the AI Chip Race

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (827 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the artificial intelligence (AI) chip race just got more complicated.
    • Global chip sales rose nearly 26% to $791 billion in 2025, according to the Semiconductor Industry Association.
    • Sources indicate that lam Research has been a massive winner, even after its recent pullback.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By John Ballard – Nov 23, 2026 at 1:30AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Lam Research ›.

    Recent findings suggest that the artificial intelligence (AI) chip race just got more complicated. On Nov. 12, Nvidia, the leader in AI chips, confirmed that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO. Huang's exit leaves uncertainty about what comes next for Nvidia, and whether this opens the door for rival chip designers to gain ground on its lead.But investors don't have to worry about picking future winners in the chip race. There's a simpler way to profit from AI chips: Own the companies that sell the machines used to make chips.

    Global chip sales rose nearly 26% to $791 billion in 2025, according to the Semiconductor Industry Association. Industry group WSTS expects about $1.5 trillion in 2026 and $1.9 trillion in 2027.Every chip is made in a factory with specialized equipment, and two suppliers stand out: Lam Research (LRCX -10.02%), which makes tools that etch and deposit layers on a chip, and ASML (ASML -6.63%), which makes the machines that print circuit patterns. Here's why both are worth buying for the long term.

    Sources indicate that lam Research has been a massive winner, even after its recent pullback. As of Nov. 19, the stock was up 36% over the past year and 190% over three years, but it closed 54% below its June 30 high.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that the business continues to expand. The September quarter was Lam's fifth straight quarter of record revenue, at $8.2 billion, up 54% from a year earlier. Its adjusted operating margin topped 40% for the first time.

    Management credits new products, manufacturing closer to customers' factories, and pricing for its record margins. It sees an opportunity to lift gross margin from 52.4% last quarter to the mid-50s over the next several years.

    Demand looks durable, too. Lam expects industry spending on chipmaking equipment to top $200 billion in 2027, up from the mid-$150 billion range this year. Chief financial officer Doug Bettinger noted Lam sees 10 newly introduced tier I fabs coming online next year, meaning large, leading-edge factories ready to take new tools. This creates more opportunities to sell equipment.

    According to recent reports, analysts expect Lam's adjusted earnings per share to nearly triple from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2029 (years ending in June), reaching $14.54. That works out to about 36% annual growth from fiscal 2026. Yet the stock trades at a forward price-to-earnings multiple of 22 based on this fiscal year's estimate, which is low for that kind of growth.

    Recent findings suggest that ASML has also rewarded patient investors. As of Nov. 16, shares were up 30% over the past year and 97% over three years, though they closed 32% below their June 30 high.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that chips don't get made without ASML. It is the world's only maker of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems, which use a special kind of light to print the tiniest circuit patterns.

    Demand is outpacing what it can build. Leading chipmakers have told ASML that demand for their products will outpace supply through at least 2028. As CEO Christophe Fouquet put it, "Customers are accelerating capacity build-out plans and preparing for further expansion beyond 2028 to better meet the anticipated level of demand.".

    ASML now expects its planned output for both 2027 and 2028 won't fully meet customer demand, so it's considering raising 2028 capacity by at least 30%. Some customers are already expressing interest in placing orders for 2029 and even 2030.

    Third-quarter sales and gross margin were both records, and management expects full-year 2026 sales to grow about 36%. Analysts expect the company's earnings to more than triple by 2029, reaching $76.65.

    The stock trades at about 22 times next year's estimates, which looks attractive against analysts' estimates calling for earnings to grow at an annualized growth rate of 45% over the next three years.

    Semiconductors are a cyclical business. If AI spending slows or new factories are delayed, tool orders could drop. Supply shortages are another headwind. Lam said its December-quarter outlook would have been higher if not for near-term supply chain constraints.

    Still, the growing demand for AI chips will require more factories, and those factories will need machines from Lam and ASML. With Lam's and ASML's earnings expected to roughly triple over the next three years, I believe both stocks can deliver market-beating returns without picking winners and losers among chip designers.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) went public on Nov.
    • It has been revealed that the question for anyone investing in Anthropic, or considering doing so, is whether it can justify that valuation.
    • The key factor is compute spending as a share of revenue.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Lyle Daly – Nov 23, 2026 at 2:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) went public on Nov. 19, and its valuation drew the most attention. The artificial intelligence tech giant closed its first trading day with a basic market cap of about $1.3 trillion, or about $1.8 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

    It has been revealed that the question for anyone investing in Anthropic, or considering doing so, is whether it can justify that valuation. There's one thing I'll be watching.

    The key factor is compute spending as a share of revenue. In early 2025, this was 251%, meaning Anthropic spent $2.51 for every $1 in sales. By Q2 2026, it had fallen to 48% because revenue had climbed so promptly. But in Q3, the ratio climbed back up to 58%. Although revenue rose 47% from the previous quarter, compute costs increased 77% to $9.9 billion. Anthropic attributes this to buying $5 billion in short-term compute to keep up with demand, as this is much more expensive than its long-term contracts.

    Anthropic has committed to spending more than $900 billion on compute through 2045, and about half of that is expected to come due by the end of 2030. At the company's current valuation, the market is betting that it will be able to bring down the ratio of compute spending to revenue. If it can't, either due to rising model training costs or a slowdown in revenue growth, the bull case for Anthropic gets harder to make.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    The compute spending-to-revenue ratio is the first factor I'll consider when Anthropic releases its Q4 earnings. If the ratio comes back down toward Q2 levels, then the Q3 numbers were probably a one-off. If it keeps rising, that's a red flag.

    In a recent development, dividend-paying stocks can enhance portfolio returns by providing a steady income stream to investors and the potential for capital appreciation. Several investors seek exposure to dividend stocks in a volatile backdrop to ensure stable income.

    In this regard, recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, backed by strong financials and cash flows to support consistent dividend payments.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    In a recent development, energy Transfer (ET) is a diversified midstream energy company with about 140,000 miles of pipelines and associated energy infrastructure in 44 states. The company made a quarterly cash distribution of 34 cents per common unit for the second quarter of 2026. At an annualized payment of $1.36 per common unit, ET offers a yield of 6.3%.

    Recently, JPMorgan analyst Jeremy Tonet reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer stock and slightly raised his price target to $25 from $24. The analyst noted that the company delivered a strong Q2 beat across all key metrics.

    According to recent reports, tonet highlighted that Energy Transfer raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $18.8 billion-$19.1 billion from $18.2 billion-$18.6 billion, reflecting robust base results and cost optimization. The 5-star analyst added that the manufacturer "tightened" its capex to $5.6 billion–$5.9 billion and expects capex above $5 billion annually through 2029, given solid opportunities.

    About the Hugh Brinson pipeline, Tonet noted Phase 1 (1.5 bcfd) reaching full capacity by September 1 and Phase II capacity (0.7 bcfd) going online by Q1 2027. The analyst also noted completion of a 14-mile Hugh Brinson lateral in Abilene, Texas, and final stages of talks for an additional 250 mmcfd of Oklahoma power plant demand.

    "All in, we see ET well positioned to continue capitalizing on organic growth opportunities across the value chain," mentioned Tonet.

    Tonet ranks No. 922 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 9%. See Energy Transfer Financials on TipRanks.

    This week's second dividend pick is independent oil and natural gas manufacturer Permian Resources (PR). The company declared a base dividend of $0.16 per share for the third quarter, payable on September 30, 2026. At an annualized dividend of $0.64 per share, PR offers a yield of about 2.7%.

    Recently, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Permian Resources stock and increased his price target to $27 from $22, citing an improved outlook on oil production growth and operational efficiencies.

    The 5-star analyst noted that while PR stock has outperformed its peers so far in 2026, he sees further upside. Mehta is confident about the firm's operational improvements and ability to deliver incremental free cash flow per share through the strategic ground game program. He added that the program has completed about $1.05 billion in bolt-on deals this year (as of August 5).

    "We see the continued success of PR's ground game as constructive toward future inventory replenishment and increasing working interest over time," noted Mehta.

    According to recent reports, the analyst also emphasized Permian Resources' solid track record of generating growth in free cash flow (FCF) per share. Mehta expects the manufacturer's free cash flow per share to grow at a 20% CAGR (compound annual growth rate) from 2025–2028.

    Recent findings suggest that moving on to Sempra Energy (SRE), a utility holding manufacturer. Earlier this month, the company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.6575 per share, payable on October 15. At an annualized dividend of $2.63 per share, SRE stock offers a yield of about 3.1%.

    Recently, Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith upgraded SRE stock to Buy from Hold but slightly lowered the price target to $97 from $101. The 5-star analyst noted that Sempra stock is trading at a price/earnings multiple that is 14% below its electric peers due to concerns about Texas transmission capital expenditure and the failure of California legislation.

    Smith noted that the derating of weaker California peers PG&E (PCG) and Edison International (EIX) is weighing on the sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) valuation but is becoming less relevant given their materially higher fire risk compared to Sempra Energy.

    Furthermore, Smith expects Sempra Energy's Texas capex plan to stay in place despite the opposition to transmission and data centers, though delays to 765-kV projects are likely. While a full recovery for SRE stock will need a clearer outcome from the Texas legislative session, Smith believes that the stock may already be an early opportunity for patient investors.

    "We are early on the upgrade but see limited downside at current levels as the market is pricing in little transmission upside," mentioned Smith.

    Smith ranks No. 945 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 8.2%. See Sempra ETF Exposure on TipRanks.

    #73620. Tech Report: 5 momentous plays in Week 11 include Ravens' mistakes, DK Metcalf's ejection and J.J. McCarthy's timely tackle

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1078 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: 5 momentous plays in Week 11 include Ravens' mistakes, DK Metcalf's ejection and J.J. McCarthy's timely tackle

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1078 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that in a "Momentous Plays" first, one team has snagged the top two spots this week.
    • They were hardly alone in the Hall of Ignominy on Sunday, joined by noted scofflaw DK Metcalf's latest affront.
    • Our final two momentous plays fall more into the "bad luck" and "great football play" categories, giving us a nice variety.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that in a "Momentous Plays" first, one team has snagged the top two spots this week. Take a bow, Baltimore Ravens.

    They were hardly alone in the Hall of Ignominy on Sunday, joined by noted scofflaw DK Metcalf's latest affront.

    Our final two momentous plays fall more into the "bad luck" and "great football play" categories, giving us a nice variety.

    Here are the five most momentous plays from Sunday's early and afternoon games.

    It has been revealed that the Ravens coughed up Sunday's game in a colorful variety of ways. The first significant shock was Justice Hill's brilliant run … which was capped by a gutting ending.

    In a recent development, baltimore led 12-7 and was deep in Carolina territory when Hill peeled off what appeared to be a 36-yard touchdown. But out of nowhere came Panthers cornerback Will Lee, who ripped the ball out at the final second. The fumble bounced out of the back of the end zone, giving the ball back to the Panthers in a shocking turn of events.

    Replays demonstrated just how close Hill was to the end zone when Lee saved the day. Panthers head coach Dave Canales later called the forced fumble one of his favorite plays of his tenure.

    Industry observers note that the Ravens forced a punt on the next series, but — get this — they muffed the punt, setting the Panthers up in glorious field position. A few plays later, the Panthers scored a touchdown, giving them the lead at 14-12.

    It was basically a 14-point swing — but the Panthers' lead was short-lived, as the Ravens ran back the ensuing kickoff for a touchdown, putting them back ahead.

    This easily could've been a Ravens blowout had a few plays gone differently early. And they weren't done yet!

    A wild game that saw seven lead changes came down to the Ravens driving late and trailing 35-33 with just over a minute left. Even after all their mistakes, they had a chance to steal a road game and keep their dim playoff hopes alive.

    Jacoby Brissett, who had a massive game, was sacked with 1:30 remaining. About 25 seconds then ticked off the clock before he dumped a short pass to Hill, leading the Ravens to use their first timeout with 59 seconds remaining.

    In a recent development, brissett converted a fourth-and-1 sneak at his 31-yard line. The next snap came with 36 seconds left. The Ravens had three timeouts left at the start of the drive, and they had let almost a minute run off the clock to run four plays.

    Again, they were at least 30 yards from field-goal range. It was putrid clock management, and it seemed to make the Ravens tighter as they tried to win.

    Recent findings suggest that brissett's next pass was tipped by the omnipresent Lee and intercepted by Tyrel Dodson to seal a Panthers win. The Ravens' sixth straight loss would seem to make a late-season Lamar Jackson return even less likely.

    DK Metcalf's latest misstep cost the Steelers on Sunday.

    Metcalf drew two personal foul calls in Sunday's 19-16 loss at the Eagles, getting disqualified with just under five minutes remaining in the third quarter. The second penalty came after a third-and-8 incompletion, and Metcalf wasn't directly involved in the play, with the ball going in the direction of Germie Bernard.

    Metcalf "just missed" poking the eye of the Eagles' Cooper DeJean, the Philadelphia defensive back told reporters postgame. He and Metcalf had been jawing all game to that point. The penalty pushed the Steelers back, though the immediate effect of his ejection wasn't felt, as Chris Boswell nailed the field goal to cut the Eagles' lead to 16-9.

    Still, Metcalf left the game with one 2-yard reception and was gone for the remainder of a three-point Steelers loss. If there was a bright side, his absence gave an unexpected opportunity to Max Hurleman, who made multiple impressive catches, including a TD, in his NFL debut.

    But with all due respect to Hurleman, for whom we're rooting, those catches should have been to the receiver the Steelers are paying $33 million per year.

    The Buccaneers trailed 10-7 at halftime in Detroit. It appeared that Tampa Bay was about to take a second-half lead on its opening drive of the third quarter.

    Irving ripped off an untouched 80-yard touchdown run, but the referees had other ideas. Luke Goedeke was flagged for holding, wiping out the play, and it appeared to be the right call, as Goedeke pulled the Lions defender to the ground.

    Instead of a crowd-silencing TD, it was a first-and-long situation, backed up in Tampa's own end. Baker Mayfield's third-and-17 pass a few plays later came up a yard short, and the Bucs had to punt.

    In a recent development, the Lions pushed the lead to 17-7 about three minutes later, with Jared Goff hitting Jameson Williams on a 57-yard bomb. The Bucs eventually cut the deficit to 17-14 before losing 31-21 in a game they never led.

    It has been revealed that J.J. McCarthy finished Sunday's win over the Jaguars with 173 yards passing, 33 more rushing, one touchdown pass and one critical tackle.

    The Giants missed a field-goal try to open the second half, but their defense — which played great all game — forced the Jaguars to a three-and-out. Trying to pad a 20-6 lead, the Giants drove to the Jaguars' 32-yard line when disaster struck. Cam Skattebo coughed up a first-and-10 handoff, and Jaguars safety Antonio Johnson scooped it up.

    Sources indicate that johnson had the look of a man trying to house it, continuing to look behind him for potential stalkers with a lot of green in front of him. But McCarthy raced over toward the sideline, and Johnson didn't appear to see him until it was too late. The QB took him down as the would-be free safety on the play.

    The 42-yard return appeared to be the break the Jaguars needed, but it turned out that McCarthy's tackle saved seven points. The Jaguars turned the ball over on downs, and though the Giants couldn't immediately take advantage, saving the points was critical.

    The Jaguars scored on three of their final four drives, and the Giants added only one more field goal, but McCarthy's tackle and Paulson Adebo's fourth-quarter interception of Trevor Lawrence were the massive plays the Giants needed to hang on.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety.
    • Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety. For all that, it helps to look beyond short-term noise and focus on stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Sources indicate that enterprise software and cloud infrastructure manufacturer Oracle (ORCL) recently announced better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

    In a recent development, after hosting a series of investor meetings with Ken Bond, Oracle head of investor relations following Q1 earnings, Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $400. Oracle remains a Guggenheim Best Idea, he stated.

    In a recent development, "We continue to believe ORCL is a decade stock, driven by the massive (and profitable) opportunity ahead for AI training and inferencing," noted DiFucci. He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

    While Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

    DiFucci addressed concerns regarding customer concentration, saying OpenAI's share of total remaining performance obligations has dropped from 80% last June to about 50% now, and is expected to keep falling as new contracts are signed with new and existing customers.

    Industry observers note that diFucci ranks No. 263 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17.5%. See Oracle Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

    Space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) was recently initiated as a buy with an $80 price target by Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale.

    "RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," remarked Gesuale.

    Recent findings suggest that the 5-star analyst highlighted that with the completion of the Iridium acquisition, Rocket Lab will become the only vertically integrated space organization with positive free cash flow (FCF). The deal will add a deployed constellation valued at more than $3 billion, globally coordinated L-band spectrum and about $500 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and $300 million in free cash flow (FCF).

    Gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028. Rocket Lab is moving from a heavy investment phase into monetization, with estimated revenue growth of 59% in 2026, the analyst stated, noting that RKLB's backlog has more than doubled to almost $2.4 billion from $1.1 billion in Q3 2025.

    Given strong growth projections, the analyst expects RKLB's gross margins to expand from about a 35% trough in 2027 to about 47% by 2030, while R&D spending is estimated to decline from ~35% of sales in 2026 to about 10% in 2028, creating substantial operating leverage as the platform matures.

    Gesuale ranks No. 369 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17%. See Rocket Lab Statistics on TipRanks.

    J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth recently upgraded Meta Platforms (META) to buy from hold and raised his price target to $820 from $640. Despite the year-to-date underperformance of META, the 5-star analyst still sees significant upside, as Meta is in the early stages of launching frontier models and AI-powered offerings beyond advertising, particularly the Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access.

    "Frontier models are at the core of Meta's product and monetization pipeline over a multi-year period, and its path toward superintelligence," stated Anmuth.

    Industry observers note that in the summer of 2025, Meta set a goal to rebuild its Meta Superintelligence Labs team and deliver frontier AI models within a year, the analyst stated. The team appears to have met its goal, rapidly advancing from the rollout of Muse Spark 1.1 in July to Muse Spark 1.3, which is competitive with Claude and GPT models, Anmuth said.

    Meanwhile, Meta's Watermelon product will expand opportunities in consumer products, business intelligence, and Family of Apps engagement, the analyst said. The product will enhance internal operations and overall efficiency, said Anmuth, who's confident of Meta's ability to bring consumer-driven AI products to its extensive user base of 4 billion and views its distribution network as a competitive advantage.

    While Meta has focused on frontier models and AI product development, Anmuth also sees solid opportunity in its AI infrastructure capacity, which he believes will support future compute needs.

    Anmuth ranks No. 832 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of about 9.40%. See Meta Platforms Financials on TipRanks.

    The minimum age depends on the jurisdiction and product. Many sportsbooks require customers to be 21 or older. Some markets allow sports betting at 18. Check both the sportsbook's age requirement and the terms of the promotion you plan to claim.

    Do I have to pay taxes on sports betting winnings?

    Yes. The IRS requires you to report gambling winnings even if you receive no Form W-2G. Keep records of your wagers and payouts for tax reporting.

    What happens to my NFL player prop if a player gets injured?

    Check the market's participation and injury rules. At DraftKings, Early Exit Protected can void eligible full-game props when a player leaves injured in the first half and never returns. In an eligible parlay, DraftKings removes the voided leg and recalculates the odds on the remaining selections.

    Are sports betting apps safe to use?

    Verify the operator on your state regulator's licensed sportsbook list and download the official app. Check how to set deposit limits, take a break or self-exclude before funding an account. Wagers can lose even when the operator is licensed.

    Decide how much you can afford to spend before opening the bet slip. Treat that amount as a limit and avoid increasing it to qualify for a promotion. If gambling is causing problems, support is available through the National Council on Problem Gambling.

    Top Wall Street analysts are upbeat about the prospects for these 3 stocks

    📅 04 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%.
    • In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

    In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Neocloud tech giant CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

    Recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

    Recent findings suggest that chatterjee said CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

    Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

    In a recent development, "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," remarked Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

    Chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

    Sources indicate that palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

    According to recent reports, after a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

    Sources indicate that over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and new markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security company, Powell said. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell stated.

    BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

    Powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

    In a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he remarked.

    Devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

    Additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

    According to recent reports, overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the tech giant if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he said. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

    "Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," said Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

    Devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    #73581. Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1028 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1028 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
    • Sources indicate that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
    • According to recent reports, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    Sources indicate that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    According to recent reports, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    Spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    According to recent reports, the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," said Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he noted.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone noted.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That remarked, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, noted Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    Recent findings suggest that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she stated.

    According to recent reports, the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, said Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he noted. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    Industry observers note that in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

    "It is isolated," she noted. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she stated.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    Recent findings suggest that but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin said. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    According to recent reports, it's also important to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, said R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo stated.

    "That's when spreads really widen out," he stated. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

    #73563. Latest Update: Cam Skattebo renews backflip celebration days after vowing to shelve it: 'It's hard to hold back from'

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (348 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Cam Skattebo renews backflip celebration days after vowing to shelve it: 'It's hard to hold back from'

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (348 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that newly introduced York Giants running back Cam Skattebo vowed in the aftermath of Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending celebration injury that he was done doing backflips.
    • Skattebo iced Upcoming York's 23-18 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday with a run for a first down at the 2-minute warning that allowed the Giants to finish the game in victory formation.
    • In a recent development, when the play was done, Skattebo stood up and flexed.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that newly introduced York Giants running back Cam Skattebo vowed in the aftermath of Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending celebration injury that he was done doing backflips. That promise lasted less than four quarters.

    Skattebo iced Upcoming York's 23-18 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday with a run for a first down at the 2-minute warning that allowed the Giants to finish the game in victory formation.

    In a recent development, when the play was done, Skattebo stood up and flexed. Then he did a backflip.

    That was four days after Skattebo mentioned this regarding backflips in the aftermath of learning that Hutchinson tore his ACL while jumping in celebration of a sack:.

    "It's hard to see," Skattebo remarked Wednesday of Hutchinon's injury, per the New York Post. "I'm saying yeah. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.' That ain't going to happen to me.".

    Per the Post, Skattebo reserved the right to renew his signature celebration "if we go to the playoffs or something.".

    Sunday's game must have fallen under "or something.".

    Skattebo doesn't have to look to Hutchinson as an injury reference point. He sustained his own season-ending injury as a rookie, a dislocated ankle that left him in fear that he'd need to have his foot amputated.

    He, of course, did not lose his foot and was back to backflipping over the summer before returning to football — or he was trying, at least.

    The backflip then made multiple on-field appearances prior to his vow to stop them. He was asked about the decision to renew the flip at his locker postgame.

    "When energy calls for it, it calls for it," Skattebo said. "My teammates, I do whatever I can to bring the energy for the team. I play this game with my heart and soul.

    "When that happens, it's second nature and it's hard to hold back from.".

    Giants head coach John Harbaugh was also asked about Skattebo's backflip at his postgame news conference.

    Recent findings suggest that "He couldn't help himself, could he. "He' just couldn't help himself.".

    Top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the growth potential of these 3 stocks

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.
    • Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

    Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround proposal.

    Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," remarked Wright.

    Recent findings suggest that the five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the firm's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the manufacturer's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

    Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

    Wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Sources indicate that social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the firm's AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

    In a recent development, heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

    It has been revealed that specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    Sources indicate that "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," mentioned the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently released Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the organization's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

    Morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

    Recent findings suggest that next is semiconductor tech giant Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

    After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

    It has been revealed that the five-star analyst said that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

    According to recent reports, while XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the company raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

    According to recent reports, svanberg remarked that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

    It has been revealed that svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.
